title: Acceptance matrix for tiered availability & burn-window release gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD fragment: define a machine-actionable acceptance matrix that ties tiered availability targets (gold/silver/bronze), per-tenant error-budget burn windows, and canary exit criteria. Purpose: give Eng teams concrete pass/fail checks for progressive rollouts so automated pipelines and the Console can block or roll back based on predicted SLA exposure. Scope: hosted API and Dedicated; exclude Private (will be driven by on-prem runbooks). Deliverables: acceptance matrix CSV, telemetry spec (metrics/dimensions), CI/CD gating rules (canary traffic thresholds, probe schedule), and a short runbook for on-call playbook changes.
acceptance_criteria: Define P50/P95/P99 latency envelopes for gold/silver/bronze across 1s, 10s, 99th percentile bucketing and example request size profiles
Uptime SLOs expressed as monthly availability % by tier and corresponding monthly error budget in minutes
Burn-window rules: explicit 30m, 2h, and 24h windows with quantified burn-rate thresholds that trigger progressive rollback or traffic-shift actions
Canary exit gating: pass criteria include no >2x baseline increase in p99 latency, error-rate delta under 0.5 percentage points, and failure to breach per-tenant budget for the chosen canary cohort
Machine-readable gating config (YAML/JSON) with fields: metric, threshold, window, action, severity, and fallback model mapping

Telemetry hooks: concrete metric names and tags for Console dashboards and alerting (examples include: redwood.request.latency.p99_ms, redwood.request.errors.per_min, redwood.tenant.error_budget.used_pct)
Integration tests: CI job that simulates canary traffic and validates gating rules against synthetic load (passes/fails deterministically)
Runbook: documented escalation steps and automated rollback commands; linked in this ticket
decisions: Use three tier buckets (gold/silver/bronze) instead of continuous percentiles to simplify canary gating and customer-facing SLAs
Adopt 3 burn windows (30m, 2h, 24h) that map to different mitigation actions (immediate rollback, traffic shaping, and operational investigation)
Expose gating config via release manifest so both Hosted and Dedicated pipelines can consume the same ruleset
Default canary cohort size: 5% of traffic or up to 5 tenants (whichever is smaller) for tenant-aware rollouts
tradeoffs: Conservative thresholds reduce risk of regressions but increase false-positive rollbacks; balanced by allowing manual override for urgent patches
Per-tenant rules improve fairness but add complexity to telemetry and test harnesses; mitigated via a simplified tenant-priority field
Short burn windows detect regressions quickly but may be noisy; we pair them with a 24h window for persistent degradations to avoid knee-jerk rollbacks
